chunks: And in the narration of Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, he said:

"Three breaths while drinking are better than drinking in one breath." And he used to dislike that one should resemble al-Hīm. I said: "What is al-Hīm?" He said: "The camel." And in another hadith: "The camels."
And it is narrated: "Al-Hīm are the she-camels."
And it is narrated: "Al-Hīm is that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned."

key_terms.اسْمُ اللَّهِ: the name of Allah, mentioned over something
key_terms.الزِّمْلُ: the camel, as given in one explanation
key_terms.الشُّرْبِ: drinking or the act of consuming a drink
key_terms.الْهِيمُ: a term explained in the reports as camels or similar beings
key_terms.بِنَفَسٍ وَاحِدٍ: in a single breath without pausing
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَنْفَاسٍ: three separate breaths taken while drinking

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about drinking in three breaths and the meaning of al-Hīm?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the etiquette of drinking, stating that drinking in three breaths is better than drinking in a single breath. It also shows the Imam's dislike of resembling animals in one's manner of drinking, with variant reports explaining the term al-Hīm in different ways.
